title: Automated runbook orchestration and alert de-bursting for noisy SLO alerts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We continue to see noisy paging during transient load spikes and multi-region failover tests. Noise comes from overlapping alerts (p95 latency, error-rate, node OOM), alert bursts when a downstream region degrades, and lack of automated contextual runbook steps. This ticket will design and implement automated runbook orchestration combined with alert de-bursting (deduplication, suppression windows, intelligent thresholds) to reduce on-call fatigue and speed mean time to mitigation (MTTM).

Scope:
- Implement an alert de-bursting layer that deduplicates and groups related alerts (by request path, model, region, and root-cause tag).
- Wire Prometheus/Alertmanager + Cortex rules to emit a single incident event for multi-signal degradations.
- Build a runbook orchestrator that triggers targeted playbooks (traffic-shift, circuit-breaker engage, KV cache purge, autoscale bump) and posts suggested steps to the incident channel and PagerDuty incident.
- Automate non-destructive remediation actions with safeguards (e.g., increase batch size or enable per-model shedding) where safe.
- Add metrics to measure reduction in pages, page escalation time, and MTTM.

Non-goals:
- This ticket will not rework the entire alert taxonomy or replace PagerDuty. It will augment existing routing and runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Alert bursts caused by the same root cause across components are merged into a single incident in >= 95% of test runs.
On-call pages for SLO violations drop by >= 40% in synthetic multi-region failover tests compared to baseline.
Runbook orchestrator can execute three curated non-destructive remediation actions automatically (with audit trail) and revert them if they worsen signals.
Playbooks for 'region latency spike', 'KV-cache corruption', and 'runtime oom cascade' are available in Confluence and linked from incidents.
Relevant dashboards show new time-to-first-action and pages-per-incident metrics.
Security review completed for any automated remediation that changes traffic routing or secrets access.
implementation_notes: Add a lightweight correlation key that joins alerts by trace_id, request_path, model_id, and region. Use this key in Alertmanager grouping and the incident creation webhook.
Implement a short suppression window (30s - 3m configurable) for alerts coming from the same correlation key to avoid N-to-1 page storms.
Leverage existing runtime health signals (p95_latency, error_rate_5m, kv_cache_miss_rate) and add a composite 'SLO-violation-score' rule to trigger incients instead of many separate alerts.

Create a small orchestration service (stateless) that receives incident webhooks, runs idempotent steps (read-only validation, throttle adjustments, cache flushes), and logs actions to CloudAudit and Slack incident channel.
Add feature flags and a dry-run mode so automated actions are initially simulated in production for two weeks before being allowed to modify state.
Integrate with PagerDuty API to annotate incidents with runbook links and executed automated actions.
Coordinate with Console/Observability team to surface 'pages avoided' KPI in per-route dashboards.
runbook_steps: Incident triage: Automated classifier assigns template: 'latency-spike-region'. Triage owner (SRE) receives synthetic incident with suggested priority.
Initial checks (automated): Verify region control-plane health, check node CPU/IO, inspect recent rollout tags, query kv cache eviction rates. Report results to incident channel.

If p95_latency > 2x SLO and error_rate increase > 0.5% AND region_router_throttles > threshold then: 1) engage per-model circuit breaker for degraded models (automated, reversible), 2) enable regional load shed policy for low-priority routes.
If KV-cache corruption pattern detected: run cache consistency check, then schedule a rolling cache purge on affected hosts with 2-min backoff between hosts.
If autoscale capacity < expected and queue backlog rising: trigger autoscale policy bump (increase desired pods/gpus) with safety limit and monitor for recovery for 5 minutes before reverting.
Post-incident: attach timeline of automated steps, revert any temporary adjustments if they were automated, and create a postmortem stub if customer_impact is high or duration > 15 minutes.
If automated action fails or worsens signals, immediately roll back and escalate to human on-call.
alerting_changes: Introduce 'SLO-violation-score' derived metric that weights p95 latency, error_rate, and request_rate, used as primary Alertmanager firing condition for paging.
Group alerts by correlation_key in Alertmanager and set group_wait=30s, group_interval=3m to reduce duplicates while preserving fast response for true incidents.
Add 'noisy' label for noisy-but-low-impact alerts and route them to a dedicated Slack channel and non-paging PD service for 48-hour observation window.
Create one composite alert for multi-region failover that only pages if at least two regions show SLO-violation-score above threshold for 2 consecutive windows.
Add automated suppression for downstream errors that cascade from a known upstream maintenance window (link to maintenance schedule).
automation_safety: All automated remediation runs under a canary flag per-customer and per-model until validated for 14 days.
Actions that change traffic routing require two SRE confirmations when customer_impact = high (manual approval at first rollout).
Every automated change must emit an audit log with actor=orchestrator and a run_id, persisted for 90 days.
Rollback hooks mandatory for every automated action and monitored; automatic rollback triggers if primary signals worsen by 10% within 5 minutes.
metrics_and_observability: New KPIs: pages_per_incident, incidents_per_week_slo, mean_time_to_mitigate (MTTM), automated_actions_success_rate.
Add Grafana panels per-route showing before/after alerting volume and pages avoided using synthetic multi-region failovers.
Instrument the orchestrator with tracing and spans to link actions to alerts/trace IDs for post-incident reasoning.
Record experiment data for 30 days and run stats to ensure no regressions in customer-facing SLOs.
